outcome: No resolution, partial resolution, or bound movement was found for any of the three stated cases (uncountable first-order theories, AECs, ℵ1-saturated models of a countable theory) in the window since 26 January 2024; the only closely adjacent development is a resolution of a related-but-different Borel-reducibility question that predates the window.
summary: The bullet covers three distinct open forms of Shelah's main gap conjecture: (1) for uncountable first-order theories that are not superstable-NDOP-shallow (the general case beyond ℵ-saturated models, which Shelah already settled), (2) for abstract elementary classes (AECs), and (3) for ℵ1-saturated (or ℵ1-|T|+-saturated) models of a countable first-order theory. Searching arXiv, Google-style web search, and the relevant survey/expository literature found no proof, disproof, or partial resolution of any of these three cases dated after 26 January 2024. The most relevant-looking hit, arXiv:2308.07510 ('Shelah's Main Gap and the generalized Borel-reducibility', Moreno et al.), resolves the Friedman-Hyttinen-Kulikov conjecture on Borel reducibility of the Main Gap in generalized descriptive set theory — a related but distinct question (about the relative complexity, under Borel reducibility, of isomorphism relations for classifiable vs. non-classifiable theories in generalized Baire space), not a case of the main-gap dichotomy on the number of models as stated in the Wikipedia bullet. Moreover this paper's v1 was submitted 2023-08-15, and even its final v3 revision (2024-10-01) is a revision of pre-window work, so it would be open_stale/out-of-scope even if it counted as the same problem, which it does not (§3.1: a variant, not a restriction, of the stated question). arXiv:2305.02020 ('AEC for strictly stable') and arXiv:2304.04467 develop frame machinery for strictly stable AECs but explicitly leave the lifting-to-higher-cardinals step open and do not establish a main-gap dichotomy. arXiv:2508.06854 (Aug 2025, an expository survey on counting countable models, covering Vaught's conjecture, Martin's conjecture, and Ehrenfeucht theories) does not address the main gap or ℵ1-saturated models at all. General searches for the ℵ1-saturated countable-theory case turned up only characterizations of why it remains open (lack of a satisfactory theory of regular types/decomposition for that case) with no claimed progress. No AI system appears anywhere in this literature; all identified work is standard human mathematical/logical argument, and no source discusses machine-checked proofs, LLM-assisted derivations, or any AI-related claim in connection with the main gap conjecture in any of its three stated forms.
competing_reading: One could argue arXiv:2308.07510's Borel-reducibility result is close enough in spirit and shares enough machinery with the main gap that it should count as 'progress' in a loose sense — the paper's own title invokes 'Shelah's Main Gap' directly, and it does establish a Borel-reducibility-theoretic dichotomy that mirrors the number-of-models dichotomy in structure. But per §3.1 the test is whether it changes what a careful person would write in the stated bullet's entry (a dichotomy on the number of non-isomorphic models in given cardinalities), and it does not: it changes what one would write about a different, though historically linked, complexity-theoretic question. It is also outside the window in any case.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement explicitly proving or refuting the main gap dichotomy (I(κ,T) maximal vs. bounded by a slow-growing function) for: general uncountable first-order theories beyond the ℵ-saturated case Shelah already handled; a broad class of AECs; or ℵ1-saturated models of a countable first-order theory specifically. Absent that, the status stands as open with no change.
